TextTranscript: This lesson is called Salvation in Christ. At this point the word salvation needs little explanation. We have seen how man has been separated from God by sin. This condition is sometimes described as being lost. When a person is delivered from that lost condition he is said to be saved. Salvation then is the condition of being saved.

I am sure you can see the progression in our lessons. We looked at the Bible in lesson one how it is put together. Then the second lesson showed our need for help because of sin. The substance of the third lesson was provided by God's careful fulfillment of His promise to Abraham resulting in Jesus' death and resurrection with the offer of forgiveness for all.

I tried to emphasize that God underlined the basis on which He would accept us. Not our merit or achievement but Jesus' perfect life given and sacrificed for us. This fourth lesson presents carefully the response we must make to God's love. Jesus once looked out over Jerusalem knowing that within days he would die outside her walls and that forty years later she would be smashed to ruins by the Romans.

Looking across the great doomed city he lamented O Jerusalem Jerusalem who kills the prophets and stones those who are sent to her how often I wanted to gather your children together the way a hen gathers her chicks under her wings and you were unwilling. You can read that in Matthew 23:37. His desire for Jerusalem was so rich and generous but there was just one problem. They were to use Jesus' word unwilling.

Well Jesus has provided a wonderful life for us but we must be willing to respond to His love. We must be willing to love him in return. Remember the words from the movie The Moulin Rouge your lips may be near but where is your heart. Jesus wants our heart. At this point though it is not just a question of willingness to respond to Jesus but one of knowledge. We must know how to respond how to love Him.

You have probably heard the beautiful song from the Gospel Rock presentation Jesus Christ Superstar I don't know how to love Him. In an unbiblical setting it puts these words on the lips of Mary Magdalene but the song states a truth of exceptional importance. Most people today don't know how to respond to Jesus' love how to love Him. I want us to read some passages together to see how we are to respond to God's love for us. Then we will notice briefly some of the amazing advantages in coming to God.

We have got a different procedure with this lesson from the others. We have provided blank spaces beside the passages we will be reading so that you can write in the appropriate information. I will give you time to examine each passage and write the information. Although you will find the information in the passages cited I will be careful to provide it in my remarks as well. Why write the information out for yourself. Because it helps you personally search the passages and because it helps emphasize the points we are making. It helps you make the information yours.

Turn please to the Gospel of John chapter six verses forty-four and forty-five. That is of course the big book of John the one that contains Jesus' life Matthew Mark Luke John. In this passage some Jews were having trouble seeing how Jesus could on the one hand be part of a human family and on the other have come down out of heaven. Jesus told them in effect that they could not understand that consequently they could not come to Him unless they had let God teach them. Let's read those verses.

No one can come to Me unless the Father who sent me draws him and I will raise him up on the last day. It is written in the prophets and they shall all be taught of God. Everyone who has heard and learned from the Father comes to me. You know if you read verse 44 on its own you may think well that leaves me out. I cannot come to Jesus because I have not felt God draw me. But the very next verse tells us how God does it.

Jesus says it is written in the prophets that they will all be taught of God. Then he says that the person who has heard and learned from the Father comes to Him. That is how God draws men to Jesus don't you see. He provides for them to be taught. You need to write the two key words from verse 45 in the space. Hear and learn. They really tell of so often today people think that God is going to call them in a mysterious super spiritual way. No He calls us by having us taught about Him. Just as is happening through this study.

I am always amazed at the responsibility he gives us to listen and to learn with open hearts. The second scripture we will turn to is just a page or two further on in John chapter eight and verse twenty-four. Now immediately before this John records that Jesus told them He would be going away. And they would seek him but not find him. And Jesus said they could not go where he was going because they would die in their sins. The Jews were pretty confused about that and even wondered if he would commit suicide.

Jesus said they were not looking at things from God's point of view. Then he said and please read John 8:24 with me I said therefore to you that you shall die in your sins for unless you believe that I am He you shall die in your sins. You see the reason they could not go to heaven where Jesus was going was that they were going to die in their sins. The only way they could avoid dying in their sins or dying as condemned people was to believe in Jesus.

Before this Jesus had been speaking of the fact that He was God's Son the light which was shining from God into the world. Those people knew many of the passages you and I have been looking at. Passages in which God promised to send Abraham's descendant God's servant or Messiah into the world to save men. When Jesus came God expected people to believe in Jesus as that one. He still does. In the space provided write what God expects us to do when we hear about Jesus. That is right. Believe or believe in Jesus or something else to that effect.

I am convinced God has been careful to unfold the story of redemption in such a way that sincere people can honestly say I believe Jesus is God's Son the Savior He promised. Acts 17:30 is the next reference for us to turn to. Aren't you pleased with the greater ease with which you are finding most of the passages now. It is always exciting for me to see people becoming better acquainted with the Bible and able to find their way through it. In Acts 17 there is a speech that Paul made in Athens.

He told the people that there is one God and that he is not honored if we worship idols of wood or stone since he made all these things anyway. Then he said that God had turned a blind eye to this past ignorance but now had a specific demand of all. Let's see what it is in verse thirty. Therefore having overlooked the times of ignorance God is now declaring to men that all everywhere should repent. I am sure you see the word there that belongs on the third line. Repent.

This word is not too rare but the people who truly understand it are. Yet it commands the response that is really the turning point God is looking for in people who hear understand and believe the story of Jesus. Some people think to repent is to be sorry. No the Bible says the right kind of sorrow godly sorrow will cause us to repent. But it is not repentance. Others think repentance is changed behavior. John the baptizer who prepared the way for Jesus told the people to show from their changed behavior that they had repented. That shows that changed behavior is not repentance but results from it.

Well what is repentance. It is a change of mind a change of heart. When a person learns he sinned against God and decides to turn to God that is repentance. When a person hears about Jesus and believes that He is God's Son and he decides to accept Jesus' gift of salvation and let Jesus be his master that is repentance. You have seen the old movies. A beloved family member struggling through the night with a dangerous fever. All the family is there amidst tears and tension. Finally the fever breaks. Doctor bears the news to the family and sighs of relief and smiles abound.

Well in God's struggle for our recovery from sin sickness the fever breaks when we repent when we decide to follow Jesus to do what He requires regardless of cost or consequence. Now let's turn to Romans ten nine and ten. Of course Romans is the first book after Acts. The book of Romans is a superb treatise of salvation through grace of how God has been able because of Jesus to fully accept man in spite of man's sinfulness.

In this passage Paul shows that the story of Jesus' awesome power to save is really intensely personal and must be responded to personally. He says that there is to be not only a necessary belief in Jesus but a stated commitment to Him. Look at the passage that if you confess with your mouth Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised Him from the dead you shall be saved. For with the heart man believes resulting in righteousness and with the mouth he confesses resulting in salvation.

We earlier saw that a person must believe that Jesus is the one he claimed to be if he wants to be free. In the space write confess Jesus as Lord or something similar. By the fifth space we have two references Matthew twenty eight nineteen and Acts eight thirty five to thirty nine. We are going to turn only to the reference in Matthew and I would appreciate if you would turn to it right now. Matthew twenty eight nineteen. You will find rich reward from reading the passage in Acts in your spare time.

It is the thrilling account of how a man from Ethiopia became a follower or disciple of Jesus. The passage shows that after the man had been told about Jesus by a preacher called Philip he saw water and immediately he wanted Philip to immerse him in it. We will find out why this thought came to his mind when we read from Matthew twenty-eight nineteen. This verse tells what Jesus after he was raised from the dead told his special messengers or apostles to do. Let's read the verse.

Go therefore and make disciples of all the nations baptizing them in the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit. Well that explains why the man from Ethiopia wanted to be baptized doesn't it. Jesus had commanded it. Told him about Jesus so he must have told him that Jesus wanted people to be baptized. It also tells us what we need to write in the space be baptized. Incidentally while you are still in Matthew 28 you might read verse 20 where Jesus continues speaking about teaching them to observe all that He commanded.

Rather surprisingly baptism is a subject of considerable controversy amongst religious people. I say surprisingly because as I think you will agree after we have looked at the next few verses the Bible is pretty straightforward on the subject. We begin by seeing just how baptism was carried out in Bible times. You may be aware that in our day the words used to describe pouring or sprinkling are sometimes applied to baptism. John also was baptizing in Aenon near Salim because there was much water there and they were coming and were being baptized.

Now what according to this passage does baptism call for. I think you have got it. If you would write that in the space provided please. Much water. We are now going to see why much water was needed in order for people to be baptized. Romans six three to five will be our first source of information. Now the book of Romans you will recall is immediately after Acts which in turn follows John. John Acts Romans.

Paul begins the chapter by countering a false notion some might hold that since God accepted them through His grace they might add wholeheartedly to the sin column of their lives so as to add more to the grace column. May it never be cries Paul. Then beginning at verse three he tells them they should realize that as Jesus died was buried and raised again when they were baptized they died and were buried with Jesus. Were it not for the fact that many sincere people accept sprinkling or pouring as baptism it probably would not even be necessary to point out that baptism in the Bible is immersion.

It is pretty obvious when Paul says they were buried with Jesus through baptism. And that explains doesn't it why John needed much water in which to baptize people. But the most powerful evidence that baptism is immersion is unfortunately hidden from readers of the English Bible. Our English New Testaments are translation from the Greek language in which the New Testament was originally written. The Greek word used for baptize means plunge dip or immerse. Rather than translate the word our translators merely made an English looking word baptize out of the Greek word.

How simple it would be if they had told us that John was immersing in Aenon near Salim because there was much water there and what needless confusion could have been avoided. You might like to take a break. This is a long lesson. Then we will continue the lesson on the other side of the tape at your leisure.
